rules.statement: Don't ask for a CHANGELOG entry to be moved out of a dated version section into Unreleased unless that version has actually been tagged or released; a dated heading alone doesn't mean it has shipped.
rules.why: The version section can still be the one being written: the release tooling tags it only after the branch's work merges, so entries for that work belong there.
rules.check: Before reporting, compare the section's version with the newest release tag on the remote (e.g. `git tag`/`git ls-remote --tags`). Report only if a tag for that version already exists.

rules.statement: A Claude Code permission rule meant to guard a sensitive path (such as a `secrets` folder) matches the bare name, e.g. `Bash(*secrets*)` and `PowerShell(*secrets*)`, not a slash-separated pattern like `*secrets/*`.
rules.why: Slash patterns miss backslash paths and variants such as `ls secrets`, and how Claude Code normalizes paths before matching is unconfirmed, so the broader pattern doesn't depend on it.
rules.check: Look in `.claude/settings.json` ask/deny rules for path patterns that require a trailing `/` or a specific separator, and so would miss `\` paths or the bare folder name.

rules.statement: When documenting Claude Code permission rules that guard secrets, say that they match the command's text, so they slow down a careless read but are not a sandbox, and point to a sandbox or a PreToolUse hook for real enforcement.
rules.why: An agent that misbehaves or has been prompt-injected can get past text-matching rules, so readers must not treat them as a hard boundary.
rules.check: Look at README or changelog text that describes secret-guarding permission rules. Report it if it presents them as blocking access and doesn't name a sandbox or hook for enforcement.
